answer: Each seat leases one named bay of a living orchard trellis, valid only while the agent keeps a violet nectar feeder there and weighs it each epoch, countersigned by a neighbour. Feeders drain with the local insect population, bounded by flowers, not capital, so fresh identities cannot fake the curve of a worked bay; theirs stay full and flat. Borrowed curves fail too: two seats on one bay give identical weights, so both bonds are slashed. A sybil needs its own bay, syrup, and a person to weigh and witness each epoch, a cost scaling with identities while per-seat yield stays fixed.
